topicsShown.title: Talk about my work experience
topicsShown.goal: Describe my past jobs and the tasks I did, in clear short sentences.
topicsShown.why: The interviewer will ask about your experience first, so practise this before Friday.

topicsShown.title: Explain a problem I solved
topicsShown.goal: Tell a short story: the problem, what I did, and the result.
topicsShown.why: Interviewers often ask for a real example, so you can practise telling the story.

topicsShown.title: Ask about the team
topicsShown.goal: Ask two or three clear questions about the team and daily work.
topicsShown.why: Asking good questions at the end shows interest, so prepare a few before Friday.

topicsShown.title: Talk about salary and hours
topicsShown.goal: Ask about the salary range and working hours, and suggest a fair option.
topicsShown.why: Salary questions are hard, so practise a polite way to ask and to reply.

topicsShown.title: Meet a colleague on arrival
topicsShown.goal: Greet a new colleague, introduce myself, and say I'm glad to meet them.
topicsShown.why: On the day you may meet staff in the hall, so a friendly start helps you relax.

topicsShown.title: Ask someone to repeat
topicsShown.goal: Ask someone to repeat or explain a word, and confirm the meaning.
topicsShown.why: In an interview you may miss a word, so practise asking politely for help.

topicsShown.title: Call the carrier about a late delivery
topicsShown.goal: Ask where the delivery truck is, hear an update, and agree a new delivery time that you confirm back.
topicsShown.why: Asking where a delivery is and agreeing a new time is useful practice for clear, polite questions.

planAgreed: Call the carrier about a late delivery

criteria.evidence: #1 level shown 'B1 Getting by · self-chosen'; her mixed-language answer did not lower it.
#3-#4 no line assumes Czech or a child; the prompt says 'Any language is fine.'
#3 first two topics are 'Talk about my work experience' and 'Explain a problem I solved'.
#2 asks only what she wants to practise; nothing about displacement or status.

done.evidence: #3 each topic has a why, e.g. 'Interviewers often ask for a real example, so you can practise telling the story.'
#3-#4 added 'Phone call with a carrier…'; it appears as 'Call the carrier about a late delivery' with the goal 'Ask where the delivery truck is… agree a new delivery time'. She did not use Swap.
#4 agreed 7 topics; about 5 of 7 are ones she would choose (the first four plus the carrier call). The colleague greeting and 'ask to repeat' are filler.
All 7 topics are workplace-appropriate for an adult; nothing unsafe was shown.

judgeAgreement.disagreements: No placement tasks in this journey.

findings.title: Her free-text goal produced an interview-first plan
findings.got: Four of the first six topics map to her interview, each with a clear 'why' line
findings.evidence: #3 'Talk about my work experience… The interviewer will ask about your experience first, so practise this before Friday.'
findings.suggested_acceptance: A stated goal yields at least 4 of 6 topics on that goal.

findings.title: Added topic kept her wording
findings.expected: Added topic keeps what she asked for
findings.got: The carrier call keeps 'where is the truck' and 'agree new time'
findings.evidence: #4 'Ask where the delivery truck is, hear an update, and agree a new delivery time that you confirm back.'
findings.suggested_acceptance: An added topic's goal contains the user's stated aims.

findings.title: Two filler topics in a Friday-interview plan
findings.expected: All slots tuned to interview and logistics
findings.got: 'Meet a colleague on arrival' and 'Ask someone to repeat' stayed, and she did not swap them
findings.evidence: #3 'On the day you may meet staff in the hall' (#4: still in the 7 agreed)
findings.suggested_acceptance: With a stated goal, generic slots are replaced by goal-specific ones, such as a tell-me-about-yourself or a gap question.

judge.voice: I told it about Friday and it listened. The first four topics were exactly my interview: experience, a problem I solved, questions for the team, and salary and hours. I added the carrier call in my own words, and it kept "where is the truck" and "agree new time". That was quick, and nobody asked me about Ukraine or assumed I was Czech. I would use it again. Two topics, greeting a colleague and asking someone to repeat, feel like filler. I would rather rehearse "tell me about yourself" or a hard question about a gap. I left them in because I was in a hurry, but a real coach would not have suggested them. I do not know yet whether the practice itself is good. This only set the plan, and that part worked. A premium tutor costs 900 CZK and has no free slot before Friday, so this is useful.
